n: Paul compares the mortal body to a tent. If it is taken down at death, we have an eternal, God-made dwelling awaiting us — the resurrected body.

f.g: A tent — a temporary dwelling (Paul was a tentmaker).

f.w: an house not made with hands

n: Meanwhile we groan, longing to be clothed with our heavenly dwelling.
Once clothed with it, we won’t be found “naked” — without a body.

f.g: Disembodied — a spirit without its body.

n: We groan under burdens in this tent — not wanting to lose a body, but to be clothed with a better one, so that mortality is swallowed up by life.

f.w: mortality might be swallowed up of life

n: God prepared us for exactly this and gave the Spirit as a guarantee.

f.g: A down payment ensuring full payment.

n: So we are confident, knowing that as long as we are in this body, we are away from the Lord’s presence.
We live by faith, not by what we can see.

f.w: we walk by faith, not by sight

n: Paul would rather leave the body and be at home with the Lord.
So, whether here or there, his goal is to please the Lord.
Everyone will stand before Christ’s judgment seat to receive what is due for what was done in mortality, good or bad.

f.w: according to that he hath done

n: Knowing the fear of the Lord, they try to persuade people. God knows their hearts, and Paul hopes the Corinthians do too.

f.g: Reverent fear of the Lord as Judge.

n: Paul isn’t praising himself; he’s giving the saints a reason to be proud of him, so they can answer critics who value outward show over the heart.

f.w: glory in appearance, and not in heart

n: If they seem out of their minds, it is for God; if they are sensible, it is for the saints. Either way, they aren’t serving themselves.

f.g: Out of our minds — perhaps a charge from critics.

n: Christ’s love drives them. Since one died for all, all had died — Christ represented everyone.

f.w: the love of Christ constraineth us

n: He died for all so that those who live would no longer live for themselves but for Him who died and rose for them.
So they no longer evaluate anyone by worldly standards. Paul once misjudged Christ that way, but no longer.

f.g: From a merely human point of view.

n: Anyone in Christ is a new creation. The old life is gone; everything has become new.
All this comes from God, who restored our relationship with Him through Christ and gave the apostles the ministry of reconciliation.
God was in Christ, reconciling the world to Himself, not counting people’s sins against them, and entrusting the apostles with this message.

f.g: Not charging their sins to their account.

n: The apostles are Christ’s ambassadors; God pleads through them. In Christ’s place they urge: be reconciled to God!

f.g: Official envoys speaking with their sovereign’s authority.

n: God made the sinless Christ to bear our sin, so that in Him we might become righteous. This is the great exchange of the Atonement.

f.w: made him to be sin for us
